"""File, schema, normalization, and duplicate validation for both deck formats."""

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from utils.data_loader import FlashcardLoadError, load_flashcards
from utils.models import Flashcard


def _write_deck(tmp_path: Path, value: object) -> Path:
    """Serialize a test deck into a real temporary UTF-8 file."""
    path = tmp_path / "deck.json"
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value), encoding="utf-8")
    return path


@pytest.mark.parametrize("wrapped", [False, True])
def test_loads_both_shapes_in_source_order(tmp_path: Path, wrapped: bool) -> None:
    """The wrapper and bare-array contracts produce the same typed cards."""
    entries = [
        {"front": "  API\t", "back": " Application Programming Interface\n"},
        {"front": "CPU", "back": "Central  Processing Unit"},
    ]
    value: object = {"cards": entries} if wrapped else entries
    path = _write_deck(tmp_path, value)
    before = path.read_bytes()
    assert load_flashcards(str(path)) == [
        Flashcard("API", "Application Programming Interface"),
        Flashcard("CPU", "Central  Processing Unit"),
    ]
    assert path.read_bytes() == before


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("filename", "count", "first", "last"),
    [
        ("glossary.json", 10, "API", "VPN"),
        (
            "python_basics.json",
            8,
            "Which keyword defines a function?",
            "Which keyword imports a module?",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_existing_sample_decks(
    filename: str, count: int, first: str, last: str
) -> None:
    """Preserve compatibility with the actual, unmodified starter samples."""
    path = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "data" / filename
    before = path.read_bytes()
    cards = load_flashcards(path)
    assert len(cards) == count
    assert cards[0].front == first
    assert cards[-1].front == last
    assert path.read_bytes() == before


def test_unicode_and_utf8_bom(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """A UTF-8 BOM and literal non-ASCII text are accepted without case loss."""
    path = tmp_path / "unicode.json"
    path.write_text(
        '[{"front":"\u2003\u6708 ","back":"Stra\u00dfe"}]', encoding="utf-8-sig"
    )
    assert load_flashcards(path) == [Flashcard("\u6708", "Stra\u00dfe")]


def test_matching_fronts_with_different_backs_are_valid(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """Repeated questions do not merge their distinct expected answers."""
    path = _write_deck(
        tmp_path,
        [
            {"front": "bank", "back": "financial institution"},
            {"front": " BANK ", "back": "river edge"},
        ],
    )
    cards = load_flashcards(path)
    assert cards == [
        Flashcard("bank", "financial institution"),
        Flashcard("BANK", "river edge"),
    ]
    assert cards[0].card_id != cards[1].card_id


def test_metadata_is_ignored(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """Unrecognized card/wrapper metadata does not extend the model contract."""
    path = _write_deck(
        tmp_path,
        {"title": "Deck", "cards": [{"front": "A", "back": "B", "tag": [1]}]},
    )
    assert load_flashcards(path) == [Flashcard("A", "B")]


def test_identity_survives_rename_reorder_and_additions(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """Unchanged content retains identity independently of its deck location."""
    path = _write_deck(
        tmp_path, [{"front": "A", "back": "B"}, {"front": "C", "back": "D"}]
    )
    before = load_flashcards(path)
    renamed = path.rename(tmp_path / "renamed.json")
    assert load_flashcards(renamed)[0].card_id == before[0].card_id
    added = _write_deck(
        tmp_path,
        {
            "cards": [
                {"front": "C", "back": "D"},
                {"front": "A", "back": "B"},
                {"front": "E", "back": "F"},
            ]
        },
    )
    after = load_flashcards(added)
    assert after[0].card_id == before[1].card_id
    assert after[1].card_id == before[0].card_id
    assert after[2].card_id not in {card.card_id for card in before}


def test_missing_file(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """A missing file becomes a structured loader exception."""
    path = tmp_path / "missing.json"
    with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError, match="File does not exist") as captured:
        load_flashcards(path)
    assert captured.value.path == path
    assert isinstance(captured.value.__cause__, FileNotFoundError)
    assert str(path) in str(captured.value)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("failure", "message"),
    [
        (PermissionError("denied"), "Permission denied"),
        (OSError("device unavailable"), "Could not read file: device unavailable"),
    ],
)
def test_unreadable_file(
    tmp_path: Path,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    failure: OSError,
    message: str,
) -> None:
    """Deterministically simulate OS errors, including elevated Windows runs."""
    path = _write_deck(tmp_path, [{"front": "A", "back": "B"}])

    def fail_read(
        self: Path, encoding: str | None = None, errors: str | None = None
    ) -> str:
        """Fail at the filesystem boundary rather than relying on chmod."""
        raise failure

    monkeypatch.setattr(Path, "read_text", fail_read)
    with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError, match=message) as captured:
        load_flashcards(path)
    assert captured.value.path == path
    assert captured.value.__cause__ is failure


def test_directory_is_not_a_deck(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """A real directory read error is translated without platform assumptions."""
    with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError) as captured:
        load_flashcards(tmp_path)
    assert isinstance(captured.value.__cause__, OSError)


def test_invalid_utf8(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """Invalid source bytes report an encoding failure, not a raw decode error."""
    path = tmp_path / "bad-encoding.json"
    path.write_bytes(b"\xff\xfeinvalid")
    with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError, match="UTF-8") as captured:
        load_flashcards(path)
    assert isinstance(captured.value.__cause__, UnicodeDecodeError)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("text", ["", "   ", "not json", '[\n{"front": "A",}\n]'])
def test_malformed_json(tmp_path: Path, text: str) -> None:
    """Malformed and empty files include actionable line/column information."""
    path = tmp_path / "malformed.json"
    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    with pytest.raises(
        FlashcardLoadError, match=r"Invalid JSON at line \d+, column \d+"
    ) as captured:
        load_flashcards(path)
    assert isinstance(captured.value.__cause__, json.JSONDecodeError)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "value",
    [
        None,
        True,
        42,
        1.5,
        "text",
        {},
        {"wrong": []},
        {"cards": None},
        {"cards": {}},
        {"cards": "text"},
    ],
)
def test_invalid_top_level_structures(tmp_path: Path, value: object) -> None:
    """Only arrays and objects with an array-valued cards key are accepted."""
    path = _write_deck(tmp_path, value)
    with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError, match="array"):
        load_flashcards(path)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", [[], {"cards": []}])
def test_empty_decks(tmp_path: Path, value: object) -> None:
    """Both supported formats require at least one card."""
    path = _write_deck(tmp_path, value)
    with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError, match="at least one card"):
        load_flashcards(path)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", [None, True, 42, 1.5, "text", ["A", "B"]])
def test_cards_must_be_objects(tmp_path: Path, value: object) -> None:
    """Card positions are one-based, even after a valid preceding card."""
    path = _write_deck(tmp_path, [{"front": "A", "back": "B"}, value])
    with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError, match="Card 2 must be a JSON object"):
        load_flashcards(path)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("field", ["front", "back"])
def test_missing_required_fields(tmp_path: Path, field: str) -> None:
    """A missing field is named together with its card position."""
    entry = {"front": "A", "back": "B"}
    del entry[field]
    path = _write_deck(tmp_path, [entry])
    with pytest.raises(
        FlashcardLoadError, match=f"Card 1: missing required field '{field}'"
    ):
        load_flashcards(path)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("field", ["front", "back"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", [None, True, 42, 1.5, [], {}])
def test_wrong_field_types(tmp_path: Path, field: str, value: object) -> None:
    """Untrusted JSON is not coerced to strings by annotations or the loader."""
    entry: dict[str, object] = {"front": "A", "back": "B"}
    entry[field] = value
    path = _write_deck(tmp_path, [entry])
    with pytest.raises(
        FlashcardLoadError, match=f"Card 1: '{field}' must be a non-empty string"
    ):
        load_flashcards(path)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("field", ["front", "back"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", ["", " ", "\t\n", "\u2003"])
def test_blank_field_values(tmp_path: Path, field: str, value: str) -> None:
    """Whitespace-only fields are rejected before card construction."""
    entry = {"front": "A", "back": "B"}
    entry[field] = value
    path = _write_deck(tmp_path, [entry])
    with pytest.raises(
        FlashcardLoadError, match=f"'{field}' must be a non-empty string"
    ):
        load_flashcards(path)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("front", "back"), [("A", "B"), (" a ", " b\t"), ("STRASSE", "B")]
)
def test_duplicate_pairs_report_both_positions(
    tmp_path: Path, front: str, back: str
) -> None:
    """Identical normalized pairs are rejected rather than silently removed."""
    original = "Stra\u00dfe" if front == "STRASSE" else "A"
    path = _write_deck(
        tmp_path,
        [
            {"front": original, "back": "B", "tag": "first"},
            {"front": "other", "back": "different"},
            {"front": front, "back": back, "tag": "different metadata"},
        ],
    )
    with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError, match=r"Cards 1 and 3.*normalized"):
        load_flashcards(path)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "text",
    [
        '[{"front":"A","front":"C","back":"B"}]',
        '{"cards":[],"cards":[{"front":"A","back":"B"}]}',
        '[{"front":"A","back":"B","tag":{"x":1,"x":2}}]',
    ],
)
def test_duplicate_json_object_keys(tmp_path: Path, text: str) -> None:
    """Duplicate object keys are distinct from the allowed repeated fronts."""
    path = tmp_path / "duplicate-key.json"
    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError, match="Duplicate JSON object key"):
        load_flashcards(path)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("constant", ["NaN", "Infinity", "-Infinity"])
def test_nonstandard_json_constants(tmp_path: Path, constant: str) -> None:
    """The stdlib's optional nonfinite-number extensions are not accepted JSON."""
    path = tmp_path / "nonfinite.json"
    path.write_text(f'{{"cards":[],"metadata":{constant}}}', encoding="utf-8")
    with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError, match="Invalid JSON constant"):
        load_flashcards(path)


def test_excessive_json_nesting(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """A decoder recursion limit becomes an expected loader error."""
    path = tmp_path / "nested.json"
    path.write_text("[" * 5000 + "0" + "]" * 5000, encoding="utf-8")
    with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError, match="JSON nesting is too deep"):
        load_flashcards(path)


def test_oversized_integer_field_is_a_loader_error(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """Decoder digit limits must not leak ValueError for an invalid back field."""
    path = tmp_path / "large-number.json"
    path.write_text('[{"front":"A","back":' + "9" * 10000 + "}]", encoding="utf-8")
    with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError) as captured:
        load_flashcards(path)
    assert captured.value.path == path
    assert captured.value.detail


@pytest.mark.parametrize("failure", [ValueError("validation bug"), RuntimeError("bug")])
def test_unexpected_validation_errors_are_not_disguised(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, failure: Exception
) -> None:
    """Decoder handling must not relabel unexpected card-validation failures."""
    path = _write_deck(tmp_path, [{"front": "A", "back": "B"}])

    def broken_validation(value: object) -> list[Flashcard]:
        """Simulate an unexpected programming error after JSON decoding."""
        raise failure

    monkeypatch.setattr("utils.data_loader._parse_deck", broken_validation)
    with pytest.raises(type(failure)) as captured:
        load_flashcards(path)
    assert captured.value is failure


@pytest.mark.parametrize("valid", [False, True])
def test_loader_never_prints(
    tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str], valid: bool
) -> None:
    """A terminal adapter can choose presentation without loader side effects."""
    path = _write_deck(tmp_path, [{"front": "A", "back": "B"}] if valid else [])
    if valid:
        load_flashcards(path)
    else:
        with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError):
            load_flashcards(path)
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert captured.out == ""
    assert captured.err == ""

"""Terminal-only escaping and formatting, without changing domain text."""

from io import StringIO

import pytest

from utils.engine import QuizSession
from utils.models import Flashcard
from utils.strategies import SequentialStrategy
from utils.terminal import configure_streams, format_summary, play, show_summary


def test_string_stream_configuration_and_control_display(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """Injected streams work and displayed controls remain on one line."""
    incoming = StringIO("wrong\n")
    outgoing = StringIO()
    errors = StringIO()
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdin", incoming)
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdout", outgoing)
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stderr", errors)
    configure_streams()
    cards = [Flashcard("A\nB\tC", "Answer\rValue")]
    session = QuizSession(cards, SequentialStrategy())
    assert play(session) == "completed"
    show_summary(session.summary, cards, "completed")
    assert r"A\nB\tC" in outgoing.getvalue()
    assert r"Expected: Answer\rValue" in outgoing.getvalue()
    assert session.summary.answers[0].card.front == "A\nB\tC"
    assert errors.getvalue() == ""


def test_partial_summary_labels_duplicate_fronts_by_position() -> None:
    """Original positions distinguish missed questions that share a front."""
    cards = [Flashcard("bank", "finance"), Flashcard("bank", "river")]
    session = QuizSession(cards, SequentialStrategy())
    session.submit_answer("wrong")
    session.submit_answer("wrong")
    text = format_summary(session.summary, cards, "completed")
    assert "#1 bank; #2 bank" in text


def test_summary_programming_error_is_not_disguised(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """Expected output handling must not hide a bug in summary formatting."""
    cards = [Flashcard("A", "Alpha")]
    summary = QuizSession(cards, SequentialStrategy()).summary

    def broken_format(*args: object) -> str:
        """Represent a programming bug outside the output operation."""
        raise RuntimeError("scripted formatting bug")

    monkeypatch.setattr("utils.terminal.format_summary", broken_format)
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="scripted formatting bug"):
        show_summary(summary, cards, "eof")

# AI-Assisted Development Project Report

**Student Name:** `A***** P*****`  
**Project Title:** Flashcard Quizzer CLI  
**Date:** 2026-11-19 — approved report

## Executive Summary

The Flashcard Quizzer loads validated JSON decks, asks each card once, evaluates text answers, and reports accuracy and missed terms. Sequential, seeded random, and adaptive modes share an engine. Persistent error-balance history and optional JSON results extend the core quiz.

Development used ChatGPT/Codex through separately reviewed stages. The student questioned design choices and accepted stages based on explanations and reported evidence. Codex executed the recorded checks; acceptance does not imply independent Python inspection or physical terminal verification.

## Project Overview

### Problem Statement

Learners need repeatable practice and useful feedback without losing progress when deck files move. Invalid input and interrupted sessions should produce understandable outcomes while preserving completed answers.

### Solution Approach

Python 3.10 is the minimum target. Runtime dependencies are entirely standard-library modules; pip and venv isolate development tools. Frozen dataclasses represent cards and summaries, while Protocol defines a structural Strategy interface. As with TypeScript interfaces, annotations describe contracts without validating untrusted JSON.

### Final Features

- Core: validated decks, finite quizzes, feedback, and partial statistics.
- Addition 1: persistent adaptive learning changes future priority across sessions.
- Addition 2: seeded random sessions reproduce an order independently of history.
- Addition 3: optional JSON session export provides metadata, statistics, and missed cards.

## AI Collaboration Experience

### AI Tools Used

ChatGPT/Codex generated and refined implementation, tests, explanations, and documentation. No other assistant is claimed.

### Collaboration Workflow

Requests specified scope, behavior, evidence, and a stopping point. Follow-up questions challenged identity, duplicates, scoring, persistence, exports, and interruption behavior. Design proposals were distinguished from accepted decisions. Stage 7 presented reproduced defects before edits; approved corrections began with failing regressions. An item-by-item Codex checklist review was performed on November 19; it is not claimed as earlier human review.

### Most Valuable AI Interactions

These are documented examples rather than a student-ranked list.

#### Example 1: Durable identity and useful priority

**Context:** History initially depended on paths and cumulative mistakes.  
**AI Prompt:** Explain moves, edits, duplicates, and decreasing scores.  
**AI Response:** Proposed content identity and error balance.  
**Your Changes:** Student review rejected path dependence, front-only uniqueness, and optional context.  
**Outcome:** Normalized front/back JSON pairs are hashed; identical cards share history. Incorrect adds one, correct subtracts one with a zero floor.

#### Example 2: F1 interruption between phases

**Context:** A boundary interruption skipped pending persistence.  
**AI Prompt:** Reproduce, test first, and prevent repeated committed updates.  
**AI Response:** Added failing entry-point regressions and phase tracking.  
**Your Changes:** Student approval required uncertain writes not be blindly retried.  
**Outcome:** Pending work resumes with status 130; observed history attempts remain one.

#### Example 3: F2 failed terminal output

**Context:** Summary failure skipped writes and changed interruption status.  
**AI Prompt:** Preserve saving/export and statuses after expected output errors.  
**AI Response:** Added closed-pipe regressions and narrow terminal error handling.  
**Your Changes:** Review required independence and visible programming errors.  
**Outcome:** EOF/interruption retain 1/130. A further regression caught shutdown status 120; retiring the failed descriptor corrected it.

### Challenges with AI Collaboration

High coverage initially missed combined failure scenarios. An oversized-integer decoder exception also required a narrow fix. A test-bootstrap delimiter mistake was corrected before valid regression results were interpreted. These failures and corrections remain recorded.

## Software Engineering Practices

### Code Quality Measures

Black, isort, flake8, strict mypy, typed functions, docstrings, and structured errors support review. Final inspection found eight missing bootstrap docstrings, eight spacing errors, and F3: failed startup-warning output replaced interrupt status 130 with 1. Approved corrections followed failing regressions. File-level and extracted-bootstrap lint now pass without weakened rules; unexpected programming errors remain visible.

### Testing Strategy

Pytest covers validation, immutable snapshots, source preservation, scoring, temporary-file round trips, persistence failures, exports, conflicts, and actual-entry-point subprocesses. Random tests check membership without requiring a changed shuffle. Stage 7 used regression-first development; this is not a claim that all development followed test-driven development.

### Design Patterns Used

Strategy is listed in the supplied guide, section 1. It was chosen so ordering can change without rewriting grading or progress. QuizStrategy defines a structural Protocol; CLI composition selects an implementation, and the engine requests its permutation once. Persistence and terminal effects remain separate.

### Code Structure and Organization

main.py delegates execution. Models/loading define validated data; engine/strategies manage sessions; history owns score updates and persistence; paths validate file roles; terminal formats output; export builds result documents; CLI coordinates them.

## Technical Challenges and Solutions

### Challenge 1: Persistence without unnecessary infrastructure

**Problem:** Renaming decks should preserve progress, and learned cards should lose priority.  
**Solution:** Canonical normalized JSON pairs produce content hashes; stable sorting uses decreasing error balance.  
**AI Involvement:** Compared alternatives and tested serialization boundaries and cross-deck sharing.  
**Lessons Learned:** Content identity trades edit continuity for simple shared history; this is a documented design consequence.

### Challenge 2: Uncertain commits and failed displays

**Problem:** An interrupted replacement may already have committed, while printing can fail independently.  
**Solution:** Finalization marks attempts before invocation and continues pending phases. Only terminal write/flush errors are translated.  
**AI Involvement:** Preserved before/after evidence, including real replacement followed by interruption.  
**Lessons Learned:** An exception does not prove noncommit. Tests observe scores and attempt counts, while formatting RuntimeError remains visible.

## Code Quality Analysis

### Metrics

Production comprises 11 Python files, 1,165 physical lines including blanks/docstrings, 62 function definitions including methods, and 22 classes. Tests comprise 13 files and 2,657 physical lines. These are size measures, not authorship counts.

Post-fix Windows CPython 3.10.11 and 3.13.17 runs each passed 275 tests with one skip, using the previously isolated environments against current source. Combined coverage is 98.21%; statements are 593/602, or 98.50%, and branches are 120/124, or 96.77%. All configured quality checks passed; no numeric linting score exists.

### Self-Assessment

Student-supplied Stage 8 ratings are unchanged. Factual reasons below reflect subsequent verification; original reasons remain in the interaction log.

- **Readability: 4/5.** Clear modules and typed models; finalization/stream handling need careful reading.
- **Maintainability: 4/5.** Engine, storage, and presentation are separated; interruption complexity is documented.
- **Test Quality: 4/5.** Strong behavioral and subprocess regressions; Windows Python 3.10.11 and 3.13.17 runtime checks passed. Physical Ctrl+C and actual symlinks remain unverified.
- **Documentation: 4/5.** Detailed instructions and evidence; clean reproduction and the authoritative rubric audit are complete. Final report wording is approved; the physical test result remains pending.

## Learning Outcomes

### Technical Skills Developed

I learned that Python annotations do not validate JSON at runtime, much like TypeScript types. Protocols resemble structural interfaces.

### AI Collaboration Skills

I challenged path-based history identity, cumulative scoring, unnecessary raw export answers, and automatic result replacement. Explanations and evidence helped me assess Python details I could not independently evaluate.

### Software Engineering Insights

I learned why high coverage does not guarantee correct behavior across failure scenarios. F1/F2 provided concrete examples of the distinction.

## Reflection

### What Worked Well

Pausing between stages gave me manageable decisions to review. The process let me question behavior before accepting it.

### What Could Be Improved

Repeated review rounds were lengthy. Next time, I would provide the full rubric earlier, agree storage/export behavior before implementation, and run manual terminal checks alongside automated tests earlier.

### Future Enhancements

The student supplied no future-feature wish list. Concurrent-session merging is an optional technical possibility requiring a separately agreed design. Current next actions are review and manual verification, not an agreed feature expansion.

## Conclusion

The project demonstrates reviewed AI-assisted implementation with measurable checks and documented limits. My next workflow would establish assessment criteria earlier and combine manual and automated verification sooner. The student accepted F3/bootstrap corrections based on reported regression evidence. Report wording is approved; physical Ctrl+C remains pending; submission is not authorized.

## Appendices

### Appendix A: AI Interaction Log

[The log](ai_edit_log.md) records nine detailed stage entries with grouped follow-ups, including identity/scoring, decoder validation, snapshots, save retries, export refinements, F1/F2, and clean reproduction. This is not a count of chat turns.

### Appendix B: Code Statistics

[The final audit](final_rubric_audit.md) links commands, metrics, checklist findings, and tested-source hashes. The 98.21% combined figure is (593+120)/(602+124); historical zero-statement coverage is not submission evidence.

### Appendix C: Additional Resources

The preserved [official template](report_template.md), [design-pattern guide](design_patterns.md), and supplied [authoritative rubric](authoritative_audit_request.md) provide context. Physical Ctrl+C and real symlink checks remain unverified; they are not explicit rubric requirements. Both runtime checks passed and F3/bootstrap corrections were accepted on reported evidence. Report wording is approved; the agreed manual result remains pending.

---

**Length rule:** The authoritative rubric requires 1,000–1,500 words. The preserved template's 2,000–3,000 footer is superseded, not an unresolved conflict. Due date and submission destination were not supplied.

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from utils.data_loader import FlashcardLoadError, load_flashcards
from utils.models import Flashcard

"""Terminal-only escaping and formatting, without changing domain text."""

import json
from io import StringIO
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from utils.engine import QuizSession
from utils.history import HistoryStore
from utils.models import Flashcard
from utils.results_export import export_results
from utils.strategies import SequentialStrategy
from utils.terminal import configure_streams, format_summary, play, show_summary


@pytest.mark.parametrize("codepoint", [*range(0x20), *range(0x7F, 0xA0)])
def test_card_controls_are_literal_in_questions_feedback_and_missed_summary(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, codepoint: int
) -> None:
    """Every C0/DEL/C1 control is escaped at each card-text display boundary."""
    control = chr(codepoint)
    escaped = {9: r"\t", 10: r"\n", 13: r"\r"}.get(codepoint, f"\\x{codepoint:02x}")
    front = f"月{control}[2J café"
    back = f"答{control}[31m naïve"
    card = Flashcard(front, back)
    cards = [card]
    session = QuizSession(cards, SequentialStrategy())
    outgoing = StringIO()
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdin", StringIO("wrong\n"))
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdout", outgoing)
    assert play(session) == "completed"
    assert outgoing.getvalue() == (
        f"\n[1/1] 月{escaped}[2J café\n"
        f"Answer: Incorrect. Expected: 答{escaped}[31m naïve\n"
    )
    summary = format_summary(session.summary, cards, "completed")
    assert f"#1 月{escaped}[2J café" in summary
    assert not any(
        chr(value) in summary
        for value in [*range(0x20), *range(0x7F, 0xA0)]
        if value != 10
    )
    assert (card.front, card.back) == (front, back)


def test_ordinary_unicode_remains_readable(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    """Readable Unicode, including emoji joiners, is not ASCII-escaped."""
    card = Flashcard("月 café 👩‍💻", "Straße λ")
    session = QuizSession([card], SequentialStrategy())
    outgoing = StringIO()
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdin", StringIO("wrong\n"))
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdout", outgoing)
    assert play(session) == "completed"
    assert outgoing.getvalue() == (
        "\n[1/1] 月 café 👩‍💻\nAnswer: Incorrect. Expected: Straße λ\n"
    )
    assert "#1 月 café 👩‍💻" in format_summary(session.summary, [card], "completed")


def test_display_escaping_preserves_grading_identity_history_and_export(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, tmp_path: Path
) -> None:
    """Only presentation changes: domain values and persisted JSON stay original."""
    card = Flashcard("月\x1b[2J", "Straße\x9b31m")
    identity = card.card_id
    session = QuizSession([card], SequentialStrategy())
    outgoing = StringIO()
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdin", StringIO("wrong\n"))
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdout", outgoing)
    assert play(session) == "completed"
    assert r"月\x1b[2J" in outgoing.getvalue()
    assert r"Expected: Straße\x9b31m" in outgoing.getvalue()
    assert (card.front, card.back, card.card_id) == (
        "月\x1b[2J",
        "Straße\x9b31m",
        identity,
    )
    store = HistoryStore(tmp_path / "history.json")
    store.save_session(session.summary)
    assert dict(HistoryStore(store.path).scores) == {identity: 1}
    export = tmp_path / "session.json"
    export_results(export, session.summary, [card], "sequential", None, "completed")
    document = json.loads(export.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    assert document["missed"] == [
        {"position": 1, "card_id": identity, "front": card.front, "expected": card.back}
    ]
    correct = QuizSession([card], SequentialStrategy())
    assert correct.submit_answer("  STRASSE\x9b31m  ").correct is True
    assert correct.summary.answers[0].card == card
    history = HistoryStore(store.path)
    history.save_session(correct.summary)
    assert dict(HistoryStore(store.path).scores) == {identity: 0}
    literal = QuizSession([card], SequentialStrategy())
    assert literal.submit_answer(r"Straße\x9b31m").correct is False


def test_string_stream_configuration_and_control_display(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """Injected streams work and displayed controls remain on one line."""
    incoming = StringIO("wrong\n")
    outgoing = StringIO()
    errors = StringIO()
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdin", incoming)
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdout", outgoing)
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stderr", errors)
    configure_streams()
    cards = [Flashcard("A\nB\tC", "Answer\rValue")]
    session = QuizSession(cards, SequentialStrategy())
    assert play(session) == "completed"
    show_summary(session.summary, cards, "completed")
    assert r"A\nB\tC" in outgoing.getvalue()
    assert r"Expected: Answer\rValue" in outgoing.getvalue()
    assert session.summary.answers[0].card.front == "A\nB\tC"
    assert errors.getvalue() == ""


def test_partial_summary_labels_duplicate_fronts_by_position() -> None:
    """Original positions distinguish missed questions that share a front."""
    cards = [Flashcard("bank", "finance"), Flashcard("bank", "river")]
    session = QuizSession(cards, SequentialStrategy())
    session.submit_answer("wrong")
    session.submit_answer("wrong")
    text = format_summary(session.summary, cards, "completed")
    assert "#1 bank; #2 bank" in text


def test_summary_programming_error_is_not_disguised(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """Expected output handling must not hide a bug in summary formatting."""
    cards = [Flashcard("A", "Alpha")]
    summary = QuizSession(cards, SequentialStrategy()).summary

    def broken_format(*args: object) -> str:
        """Represent a programming bug outside the output operation."""
        raise RuntimeError("scripted formatting bug")

    monkeypatch.setattr("utils.terminal.format_summary", broken_format)
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="scripted formatting bug"):
        show_summary(summary, cards, "eof")

        """Fail at the filesystem boundary rather than relying on chmod."""
        raise failure

    monkeypatch.setattr(Path, "read_text", fail_read)
    with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError, match=message) as captured:
        load_flashcards(path)
    assert captured.value.path == path
    assert captured.value.__cause__ is failure


def test_directory_is_not_a_deck(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """A real directory read error is translated without platform assumptions."""
    with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError) as captured:

    assert isinstance(captured.value.__cause__, OSError)


def test_invalid_utf8(tmp_path: Path) -> None:

@pytest.mark.parametrize("text", ["", "   ", "not json", '[\n{"front": "A",}\n]'])
def test_malformed_json(tmp_path: Path, text: str) -> None:

@pytest.mark.parametrize(

def test_invalid_top_level_structures(tmp_path: Path, value: object) -> None:

@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", [[], {"cards": []}])
def test_empty_decks(tmp_path: Path, value: object) -> None:

@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", [None, True, 42, 1.5, "text", ["A", "B"]])

def test_duplicate_pairs_report_both_positions(

) -> None:

    path = _write_deck(
        tmp_path,

            {"front": front, "back": back, "tag": "different metadata"},

)

    with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError, match="Duplicate JSON object key"):

@pytest.mark.parametrize("constant", ["NaN", "Infinity", "-Infinity"])
def test_nonstandard_json_constants(tmp_path: Path, constant: str) -> None:
    """The stdlib's optional nonfinite-number extensions are not accepted JSON."""
    path = tmp_path / "nonfinite.json"
    path.write_text(f'{{"cards":[],"metadata":{constant}}}', encoding="utf-8")
    with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError, match="Invalid JSON constant"):
        load_flashcards(path)


def test_decoder_recursion_error_becomes_nesting_load_error(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """Translate decoder recursion deterministically, without an OS depth limit."""
    path = _write_deck(tmp_path, [{"front": "A", "back": "B"}])
    failure = RecursionError("scripted decoder recursion")

    def fail_decoder(*args: object, **kwargs: object) -> object:
        """Raise only at the JSON decoder boundary for this loader invocation."""
        raise failure

    with monkeypatch.context() as decoder:
        decoder.setattr("utils.data_loader.json.loads", fail_decoder)
        with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError) as captured:
            load_flashcards(path)
    assert captured.value.detail == "JSON nesting is too deep."
    assert captured.value.path == path
    assert captured.value.__cause__ is failure
    assert load_flashcards(path) == [Flashcard("A", "B")]


def test_excessive_json_nesting(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """Reject a real nested file whether decoding or deck validation rejects it."""
    path = tmp_path / "nested.json"
    path.write_text("[" * 5000 + "0" + "]" * 5000, encoding="utf-8")
    with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError) as captured:
        load_flashcards(path)
    assert captured.value.path == path


def test_oversized_integer_field_is_a_loader_error(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """Decoder digit limits must not leak ValueError for an invalid back field."""
    path = tmp_path / "large-number.json"
    path.write_text('[{"front":"A","back":' + "9" * 10000 + "}]", encoding="utf-8")
    with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError) as captured:
        load_flashcards(path)
    assert captured.value.path == path
    assert captured.value.detail


@pytest.mark.parametrize("failure", [ValueError("validation bug"), RuntimeError("bug")])
def test_unexpected_validation_errors_are_not_disguised(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, failure: Exception
) -> None:
    """Decoder handling must not relabel unexpected card-validation failures."""
    path = _write_deck(tmp_path, [{"front": "A", "back": "B"}])

    def broken_validation(value: object) -> list[Flashcard]:
        """Simulate an unexpected programming error after JSON decoding."""
        raise failure

    monkeypatch.setattr("utils.data_loader._parse_deck", broken_validation)
    with pytest.raises(type(failure)) as captured:
        load_flashcards(path)
    assert captured.value is failure


@pytest.mark.parametrize("valid", [False, True])
def test_loader_never_prints(
    tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str], valid: bool
) -> None:
    """A terminal adapter can choose presentation without loader side effects."""
    path = _write_deck(tmp_path, [{"front": "A", "back": "B"}] if valid else [])
    if valid:
        load_flashcards(path)
    else:
        with pytest.raises(FlashcardLoadError):
            load_flashcards(path)
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert captured.out == ""
    assert captured.err == ""

"""Terminal-only escaping and formatting, without changing domain text."""

import json
from io import StringIO
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from utils.engine import QuizSession
from utils.history import HistoryStore
from utils.models import Flashcard
from utils.results_export import export_results
from utils.strategies import SequentialStrategy
from utils.terminal import configure_streams, format_summary, play, show_summary


@pytest.mark.parametrize("codepoint", [*range(0x20), *range(0x7F, 0xA0)])
def test_card_controls_are_literal_in_questions_feedback_and_missed_summary(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, codepoint: int
) -> None:
    """Every C0/DEL/C1 control is escaped at each card-text display boundary."""
    control = chr(codepoint)
    escaped = {9: r"\t", 10: r"\n", 13: r"\r"}.get(codepoint, f"\\x{codepoint:02x}")
    front = f"月{control}[2J café"
    back = f"答{control}[31m naïve"
    card = Flashcard(front, back)
    cards = [card]
    session = QuizSession(cards, SequentialStrategy())
    outgoing = StringIO()
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdin", StringIO("wrong\n"))
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdout", outgoing)
    assert play(session) == "completed"
    assert outgoing.getvalue() == (
        f"\n[1/1] 月{escaped}[2J café\n"
        f"Answer: Incorrect. Expected: 答{escaped}[31m naïve\n"
    )
    summary = format_summary(session.summary, cards, "completed")
    assert f"#1 月{escaped}[2J café" in summary
    assert not any(
        chr(value) in summary
        for value in [*range(0x20), *range(0x7F, 0xA0)]
        if value != 10
    )
    assert (card.front, card.back) == (front, back)


def test_ordinary_unicode_remains_readable(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    """Readable Unicode, including emoji joiners, is not ASCII-escaped."""
    card = Flashcard("月 café 👩‍💻", "Straße λ")
    session = QuizSession([card], SequentialStrategy())
    outgoing = StringIO()
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdin", StringIO("wrong\n"))
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdout", outgoing)
    assert play(session) == "completed"
    assert outgoing.getvalue() == (
        "\n[1/1] 月 café 👩‍💻\nAnswer: Incorrect. Expected: Straße λ\n"
    )
    assert "#1 月 café 👩‍💻" in format_summary(session.summary, [card], "completed")


def test_display_escaping_preserves_grading_identity_history_and_export(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, tmp_path: Path
) -> None:
    """Only presentation changes: domain values and persisted JSON stay original."""
    card = Flashcard("月\x1b[2J", "Straße\x9b31m")
    identity = card.card_id
    session = QuizSession([card], SequentialStrategy())
    outgoing = StringIO()
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdin", StringIO("wrong\n"))
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdout", outgoing)
    assert play(session) == "completed"
    assert r"月\x1b[2J" in outgoing.getvalue()
    assert r"Expected: Straße\x9b31m" in outgoing.getvalue()
    assert (card.front, card.back, card.card_id) == (
        "月\x1b[2J",
        "Straße\x9b31m",
        identity,
    )
    store = HistoryStore(tmp_path / "history.json")
    store.save_session(session.summary)
    assert dict(HistoryStore(store.path).scores) == {identity: 1}
    export = tmp_path / "session.json"
    export_results(export, session.summary, [card], "sequential", None, "completed")
    document = json.loads(export.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    assert document["missed"] == [
        {"position": 1, "card_id": identity, "front": card.front, "expected": card.back}
    ]
    correct = QuizSession([card], SequentialStrategy())
    assert correct.submit_answer("  STRASSE\x9b31m  ").correct is True
    assert correct.summary.answers[0].card == card
    history = HistoryStore(store.path)
    history.save_session(correct.summary)
    assert dict(HistoryStore(store.path).scores) == {identity: 0}
    literal = QuizSession([card], SequentialStrategy())
    assert literal.submit_answer(r"Straße\x9b31m").correct is False


def test_string_stream_configuration_and_control_display(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """Injected streams work and displayed controls remain on one line."""
    incoming = StringIO("wrong\n")
    outgoing = StringIO()
    errors = StringIO()
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdin", incoming)
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdout", outgoing)
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stderr", errors)
    configure_streams()
    cards = [Flashcard("A\nB\tC", "Answer\rValue")]
    session = QuizSession(cards, SequentialStrategy())
    assert play(session) == "completed"
    show_summary(session.summary, cards, "completed")
    assert r"A\nB\tC" in outgoing.getvalue()
    assert r"Expected: Answer\rValue" in outgoing.getvalue()
    assert session.summary.answers[0].card.front == "A\nB\tC"
    assert errors.getvalue() == ""


def test_partial_summary_labels_duplicate_fronts_by_position() -> None:
    """Original positions distinguish missed questions that share a front."""
    cards = [Flashcard("bank", "finance"), Flashcard("bank", "river")]
    session = QuizSession(cards, SequentialStrategy())
    session.submit_answer("wrong")
    session.submit_answer("wrong")
    text = format_summary(session.summary, cards, "completed")
    assert "#1 bank; #2 bank" in text


def test_summary_programming_error_is_not_disguised(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """Expected output handling must not hide a bug in summary formatting."""
    cards = [Flashcard("A", "Alpha")]
    summary = QuizSession(cards, SequentialStrategy()).summary

    def broken_format(*args: object) -> str:
        """Represent a programming bug outside the output operation."""
        raise RuntimeError("scripted formatting bug")

    monkeypatch.setattr("utils.terminal.format_summary", broken_format)
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="scripted formatting bug"):
        show_summary(summary, cards, "eof")
